title: quant-kernel-packer-and-dynamic-alignment-for-int8-throughput
author: Samir Desai
description: Motivation: Reduce kernel launch overhead and improve vector unit utilization for INT8 and mixed INT8/FP8 paths on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs by packing quantized micro-tiles into contiguous dispatch buffers and aligning KV-cache slices to the kernel alignment size. This PR introduces a "quant-kernel packer" subsystem that performs runtime packing of small token micro-batches and a dynamic-alignment allocator for KV cache windows so kernels hit coalesced memory accesses more often. Summary of changes: - New runtime component runtime/quant/pack_kernel.cc and header pack_kernel.h implementing packing strategies and a small cost-model to decide when to pack vs. dispatch directly. - KV cache allocator modifications in runtime/kv/kv_allocator.cc to support alignment hints and to pre-shift slices by block-size to avoid unaligned loads for 2D KV tiles. - Kernel ABI changes: added a small descriptor struct (packed_descriptor_t) used only by quantized microkernels to describe contiguous sub-buffers; backward-compatible with non-packed kernels. - Scheduler integration: scheduler/batching/packer_integration.cc adds a small decision hook that can pack across in-flight micro-batches when the model's transformer width and token length indicate benefit. - Tests: unit tests for packing logic (tests/quant/test_packer.cc), integration benchmarks (benchmark/quant/packer_throughput.py), and nightly perf job entry. Design goals/checklist: - [x] Avoid extra device->host roundtrips and keep all packing on-device when possible. - [x] Make packing opt-in by model profile, default off for small models. - [x] Keep ABI changes local to quant path to minimize regression surface. - [x] Provide performance telemetry (metrics: quant.packer.pack_ratio, quant.packer.cpu_overhead_ms). Performance results (internal bench across p3.8xlarge and comparable AMD rigs): - Baselines used: current main INT8 path without dequant fusion or kernel packing. - Micro-batch throughput improvement: +18% median for decoder-only models at seq_len=128, +11% at seq_len=512. - Median p50 latency impact: +2.5% (within SLA for throughput optimized configs). - Token-per-second normalized cost improvement: ~12% for mixed INT8/FP8 models with prefix-KV heavy workloads. Compatibility notes: - This PR does not change non-quantized kernel paths. - Default behaviour remains the same; a new model profile flag "enable_kernel_packing" controls activation. - SmoothQuant and dequant-fusion code paths were considered: the packer detects fused-dequant kernels via descriptor and routes packed buffers to the fused path when available to avoid extra dequant copies. Commits summary: - "add quant kernel packer and runtime cost model" - "kv allocator: alignment hint and block-shift support" - "scheduler: packer decision hook and config flag" - "unit tests and benchmark scaffolding" Files changed (high-level): - runtime/quant/pack_kernel.cc, runtime/quant/pack_kernel.h - runtime/kv/kv_allocator.cc, runtime/kv/kv_allocator.h - runtime/quant/descriptors.h (packed_descriptor_t) - scheduler/batching/packer_integration.cc - tests/quant/test_packer.cc - benchmark/quant/packer_throughput.py - docs/quant/packing.md (design doc and activation guide) Migration/upgrade notes: - No customer-facing API changes. For Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments, packer activation is gated behind a runtime config flag (redwood.runtime.quant.enable_kernel_packing) that can be toggled per-cluster. CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration benchmarks: flaky on first run (GPU memory allocator race) -> fixed by kv_allocator guard; subsequent runs pass - Lint: pass - Nightly perf job: included the new benchmark; results uploaded to perf dashboard Reviews & conversation: see review_comments field for detailed thread. Merge strategy: squash and merge. Related Linear tasks: ["ENG-8215", "ENG-8340"]. Related Jira: ["SUP-4121"]

review_comments: Arielle Park (reviewer): Nice work. Can you clarify memory lifetime semantics for packed buffers? If a kernel faults we need a safe fallback path to un-packed dispatch.

Samir Desai (author): Reply: packed_descriptor_t uses ref-counted device buffers; packer provides a fallback path that returns an un-packed buffer to the normal scheduler when allocation fails or when the cost-model prefers direct dispatch. Added unit test to cover kernel fault fallback.

Jordan Li (reviewer): Suggestion: expose a small perf counter for pack_ratio by model id so customers can reason about activation impact. Also please add a guard for tiny models (< 2M params) to avoid regressions.
Samir Desai (author): Reply: added quant.packer.pack_ratio and quant.packer.reject_reasons metrics. Also updated model profile gating to default-off for models < 2.5M params.
Marina Kovacs (approver): Verified p3 runs and reviewed safety checks. Approve with one nits left around header comments.

CI Bot: integration tests failed on first run due to allocator race (observed OOM on AMD rig). Cause: alignment hint + lazy-backend allocation ordering. Fix: add kv_allocator guard and retry; re-ran CI and all checks passed.
